title: Global trends of pandemic-prone and epidemic-prone disease outbreaks in 2024
snippet: In 2024, events of concern related to Oropouche virus disease were registered in 11 countries and territories, all of them reported in the Americas, particularly in Latin America and the Caribbean. While no outbreaks were reported in 2023, 2024 was characterised by the emergence of this disease in areas where it had not been previously detected, such as Bolivia, Cuba, the USA and Canada.8 9 [...] About 90% of the outbreaks in 2024 were associated with COVID-19, dengue, yellow fever, Oropouche virus disease and influenza (linked to identified zoonotic or pandemic influenza virus). Although disease outbreaks can affect any country anywhere, they tend to disproportionately occur in countries facing many other socio-economic development, climatic and humanitarian challenges. One of the most frequently recorded diseases in 2024 was the Oropouche virus. According to WHO, its spread has extended beyond its traditional geographical boundaries, driven by a combination of climate change, deforestation and rapid, unregulated urban expansion. title: Clinical Overview of Oropouche Virus Disease | Oropouche | CDC
snippet:
Prior to 2000, outbreaks of Oropouche virus were reported in Brazil, Panama, and Peru. Evidence of animals being infected was also noted in Colombia and Trinidad during this time. In the last 25 years, cases of Oropouche have been identified in many countries, including Argentina, Bolivia, Brazil, Colombia, Ecuador, French Guiana, Panama, and Peru. One child was found to be infected in Haiti in 2014. [...] In late 2023, Oropouche virus was identified as causing large outbreaks in endemic areas and new areas in South America. In June 2024, Cuba reported its first confirmed Oropouche case. For the latest information, see Countries and Territories with Recent or Previous Oropouche Virus Transmission. Currently, there is no evidence of local transmission in the United States.

## Clinical features [...] ## On This Page

## Oropouche

Oropouche virus spreads primarily through the bites of infected biting midges. Travelers to the Caribbean and South and Central America are at higher risk.

title: Oropouche virus disease
snippet:
Prior to late 2023, Oropouche virus disease was reported in Brazil, Bolivia, Colombia, Ecuador, Haiti, Panama, Peru, Trinidad and Tobago, French Guiana and Venezuela; most cases were reported near the Amazon rainforest area. However, since December 2023, there has been an increase in the number of cases reported, including in areas where transmission had not been previously documented. [...] In 2024, locally transmitted Oropouche virus disease was reported in seven countries in Latin America and the Caribbean: Brazil, Bolivia, Colombia, Cuba, Guyana, Peru and the Dominican Republic (2–5).  Additionally, Oropouche virus disease cases were reported among travellers returning from countries with local transmission to the United States, Canada, Spain, Italy and Germany (6,7).

## Transmission [...] The virus is transmitted to people through the bite of an infected insect, usually biting midges but also possibly by mosquitoes. It is thus referred to as an arthropod-borne virus (arbovirus). Prior to late 2023, reported cases of Oropouche virus disease were limited to South America, mostly near the Amazon rainforest, and the Caribbean.
